changes.summary: Waiver claims work again during the waiver window — every claim was being refused as "player locked", and Free Agents offers Add on every free agent again.
Free Agents no longer offers a claim on a player you're viewing in the other conference — claims always file into your own.
The homepage hero now runs the same weekly rotation as the other leagues: game day, the Tuesday recap, the Pecking Order, waivers and The Gauntlet, cast with your own players.
Rosters are now the full roster page: this week's matchup, opponent rank, season points and projection for every player, plus Release, IR and trade-block actions on your own team.
The ⋮ player menu on Rosters opens again after you switch to another team from the crest row, instead of going dead until you reload.
Live Scoring is here: both of your games first, then every matchup by division, with win odds, box scores and a scoring ticker.
changes.headline: Live Scoring comes to Archie's
changes.lede: Your two games up top, then every matchup in all nine divisions — live win odds, box scores and a scoring ticker, all on one page.
changes.imageAlt: Archie's Live Scoring page: division filter pills above a featured matchup card with projections and a win-odds bar, and smaller matchup cards below.

changes.summary: Standings now has three tabs: Division, MAD (the MAD Power 99 playoff race, 30 teams in) and All-Play, plus PA, streak and division records.
Archie's has a new look: black header and footer, the wordmark's sky blue as the accent, and sharper text contrast in light and dark.
New: the Trade Builder. Pick players from your roster and a division rival's, check the value balance, and send the offer, or start one from the ⋮ menu on Rosters.
Maverick's 2016–2024 seasons show their original Mel Gibson art again instead of today's logo, and it's now Maverick's default Throwback Week look.
The player card's Season Results table is readable again — upcoming weeks and byes no longer vanish in dark mode, and it fits a phone without scrolling sideways.
Declaring a contract works again — it was failing with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cancelled')" and never filed.
The rest of the player card's faded labels (stats, details, section titles, "Rostered by") are now easy to read in both light and dark mode.
On a phone, Coach view roster cards keep the matchup and the stats line on one line each — a 10:00 kickoff or a two-digit rank no longer bumps the rank or the average onto a line of its own.
Live Scoring: Throwback teams now wear their era colours, and when two teams share a colour your own team keeps it.
The Owners' Poll has its own page: vote, then see the full owners' rankings. Claude's results post links there, and Pecking Order no longer mixes in poll results.
Prime Video games now show the new Thursday Night Football shield (white in dark mode); on Set Lineup, square network logos like NBC, ABC and FOX draw a little larger.
Tap any player in a Live Scoring matchup to see every stat and the points it earned under your league's scoring.
changes.headline: See exactly where every point came from
changes.lede: Live Scoring now breaks each player's score down stat by stat. Tap a player in any matchup and a sheet shows his passing, rushing, receiving and kicking line with the points each one earned under your league's own scoring rules, adding up to the official total.
changes.imageAlt: A Live Scoring matchup with Josh Allen's stat sheet open, listing passing yards, interceptions, rushing yards, rushing touchdowns and fumbles with the points for each and a 16.46 total.

changes.headline: Every stat behind every score
changes.lede: Live Scoring now opens a stat sheet for any player you tap: his full line for the week, stat by stat, under the official score.
changes.imageAlt: A Live Scoring matchup with a player's stat sheet open, listing his passing, rushing and fumble stats above the official total.

changes.summary: Buttons and "see more" links now look and behave the same on every page, and no longer turn red and underlined when you hover them.
The draft room's countdown banner is readable in every state again, light and dark — its white text no longer sits on pale amber, green or grey.
The draft room's countdown banner is readable in every state again, light and dark — its white text no longer sits on pale amber, green or grey.
Buttons now wear the AFL red instead of the shared blue, in light and dark mode.
Buttons now wear the Best Ball emerald instead of the shared blue, in light and dark mode.
In dark mode, blue pills, tags and highlighted tabs are a deeper blue, so their white text is easy to read.
In dark mode, sky-blue pills, tags and highlighted tabs now carry black text instead of hard-to-read white.
Homepage heroes now wear Archie's black and sky blue instead of navy.
Heroes and buttons now wear Best Ball's emerald, with text that stays readable in dark mode.
In dark mode, buttons and tags in the league colour now use dark text where white was hard to read.
The Set Lineup button turns a deeper green once your lineup is saved, so its text is easy to read.
The homepage now shows the MAD Power 99 playoff race: all 30 qualifiers as crest tiles by tier, with a link to the full standings.
Team crests that were hard to see in dark mode now get a thin white outline, so every team stays easy to spot.
Shared Schefter posts now show their preview image with the league logo when posted to chat or social apps.
The Pecking Order now shows your own league's team names and logos.
Owners' Poll posts in League News now open the right page instead of a not-found page when you browse the league at mfl.football.
The Read the Rulebook button on Ask Roger is easier to read in dark mode.
